The image shows a single mango leaf against a white background. The leaf itself is mostly green but has several areas of damage and discoloration. There are small, scattered brown spots across the leaf surface, which are characteristic of Anthracnose infections. More significantly, the tip of the leaf is necrotic, brown, and appears to be dying or drying out, which is a classic symptom of Die Back disease, where the plant tissue dies from the tip inward. The combination of spotting and the prominent tip necrosis makes Die_Back the most fitting diagnosis. The symptoms do not align with Powdery Mildew (white, powdery spots) or Sooty Mould (black, fungal growth).
